newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai trade sees gold demand up after India holiday.
newsitem.headline: Dubai trade sees gold demand up after India holiday.

text.p: Dubai's gold traders said on Sunday they expected demand to rise in the next week after national holidays are over in the Indian subcontinent, the world's largest gold market.
A Dubai-based refinery said it had doubled its output this month of the benchmark Ten Tola Bar (TT) to meet the forecast rise in demand ahead of the Indian festival season.

"Last week we had less demand compared to the week before because of the holidays in India," one trader said. "From Tuesday onwards, we will see demand again in the market. Gold prices are still within a comfortable range."
India and Pakistan this week celebrated 50 years of independence from British rule. Indian banks are scheduled to return to work on Tuesday, traders said.
Dubai is the main source of gold imported to India. Around three quarters of Dubai's gold imports are re-exported to India, the world's second most populous country after China.
India's main festival and wedding season begins in September following the annual monsoon rains, when farmers harvest crops.

Recently weaker gold prices on the international market have buoyed demand for the precious metal, particularly from Dubai traders wanting to take advantage of low prices ahead of the usually busy festival season.
Traders said investors had also been buying on expectations that prices would move higher.
International spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $326.50/327.25 an ounce, versus $326.20/$326.70 a week earlier.
Dubai traders see gold trading over the next week within a range of $323 and $332 an ounce.
Dubai's benchmark TT bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted on Sunday at 4,520 dirhams ($1,232), up from between 4,505 and 4,515 dirhams ($1,227-$1,230) last week.

Emirates Gold refinery manager Samir Abdel-Aziz Kharsa said his factory lifted output in August to about 1,800 TT bars a day from some 1,000 to meet growing demand in the absence of supplies from Europe.
"There is an increase in demand because prices are down and because in Switzerland they are taking their annual holiday," Kharsa told Reuters.
He said Emirates Gold did not import gold directly, but converted gold imported by Dubai-based traders into TT bars.
"This month, we are working day and night to meet demand," said Kharsa.
